survivingClaim: Record lane; no attack; nothing about zeros of zeta. The thin prime deletion control DEL_b (greedy deletion with counting function L(x) = int_2^x t^(b-1) dt/log t) has Lambda_F >= 0 and F = zeta(s)(s-b)W(s) on Re s > max(b-eta, b/2) with W zero-free, hence a simple real zero at b for every b in (1/2,1). This holds relative to a short-interval prime theorem (Huxley 1972 asymptotic for theta > 7/12; primary text not opened by anyone), with the orientation remark repaired as in E1. At half density the factor is (s-b)^(1/2), a branch point. The upper bound D <= 0, the tail bound and the Tier 0 bounds are unconditional; the Tier E width is relative to the explicit pi(x) - li(x) bounds. Float64 cases b = 0.6, 0.85 (lane) and b = 0.7 (this referee) agree: not zero, not zeta, exponent 1 at density one and 1/2 at half density. Statement O v3 exists as a separate file with the c9 file unchanged; the map (180 to 182 rows) and engine counts (1,649 nodes, 14,980 scored) match the files.

lesson: A control proved relative to a classical theorem can get its second referee file, but its label stays "relative to" until the primary text is opened. A numerical enclosure resting on an explicit bound must name the bound: swapping Trudgian's for the Fiori-Kadiri-Swidinsky form widens the DEL Tier E interval from about 4% to a factor 73 to 165.
